product.amstrad-pc2286.summary: The middle tier of the PC2000 series brought professional applications to the 286 and expandable memory.
product.amstrad-pc2286.history: Announced in September 1988, the PC2286 occupied the professional middle tier between the PC2086 and PC2386. Amstrad offered DOS 4.0 and Windows 286, with OS/2 envisaged after memory expansion. In France, the 1 November 1988 price list asked 12,890 francs excluding VAT for the DD 12 MD with two floppy drives and a 12-inch monochrome monitor. On manufacture, the April 1989 brochure states assembly in Korea; Dataquest in September 1989 names GPT in Kirkcaldy, Scotland. The correspondence between factories and production batches remains unresolved.
product.amstrad-pc2286.warning: Historical card under research; it does not enable creation of a validated machine in BluMach.
product.amstrad-pc2286.technical.market: The series targeted professional users. Computerwoche reported its announcement on 30 September 1988; this does not establish the first sale date in each country.
product.amstrad-pc2286.technical.configu: The range offered a choice between floppies and a hard disk. The brochure lists two high-density 3.5-inch drives or one drive alongside a 40 MB disk.
product.amstrad-pc2286.technical.memory: Expandable memory allowed more demanding applications. The brochure documents a 12 MHz 80286, 1 MB of parity RAM expandable to 4 MB on the motherboard, and LIM 4.0 expanded memory. The optional 80287 coprocessor had a dedicated socket.
product.amstrad-pc2286.technical.video: The display did not require an additional card. The brochure documents integrated VGA and compatibility with EGA, CGA and Hercules.
product.amstrad-pc2286.technical.expansi: The number and type of slots determine expansion options. The April 1989 brochure contradicts itself: p. 5 specifies five 16-bit slots, while the back-cover table lists four 16-bit slots and one 8-bit slot. Both versions are retained.
product.amstrad-pc2286.technical.interfa: Printers and communications had dedicated connections. The documentation lists a bidirectional parallel port, RS-232 and a connector for external drives or tape.
product.amstrad-pc2286.technical.firmwar: Two owner contributions allow the dumps to be compared. The four 32 KiB ROMs, 40189-2 through 40192-2, match byte for byte after decoding the 2023 hexadecimal attachments; the 2026 files include a 64 KiB system BIOS and 16 KiB video BIOS. This does not confirm each chip's physical location.
product.amstrad-pc2286.technical.verifie: The available evidence supports further research. Sizes, hashes and firmware matches were checked; BluMach 88f74ba3 does not register a dedicated pc2286 machine.
product.amstrad-pc2286.technical.limitat: Preserved BIOS files do not demonstrate that BluMach can boot this computer. A dedicated model, physical cross-checks and boot tests are still needed; the new dumps have neither been executed nor scanned for malware. A publishable image awaits clear rights.
product.amstrad-pc2286.technical.brochur: Amstrad PC2000 Series, April 1989, pp. 3, 5 and 7 and back cover: configurations, hardware, assembly and two different slot descriptions.
product.amstrad-pc2286.technical.prices: Tarifs gamme PC2000, 1 November 1988: indicative French prices excluding VAT, with monitor and configuration specified.
product.amstrad-pc2286.technical.press: Computerwoche, Amstrad kommt mit PC-Serie 2000, 30 September 1988: announcement and each model's position.
product.amstrad-pc2286.technical.oem: Dataquest, Amstrad Plc, ESAM Volume I, September 1989, report 0004839, pp. 9–10: GPT in Kirkcaldy for PC2286/PC2386; this differs from Korean assembly stated in the brochure.
product.amstrad-pc2286.technical.firmwar: VCF, Amstrad PC 2286 thread, pages 4 and 7: 2023 and 2026 attachments preserved and compared; redistribution rights are unknown.
product.amstrad-pc2286.technical.source: BluMach source inspection at 88f74ba3: machine table and m_amstrad.c. This documents code presence, not verified operation.
product.amstrad-pc2286.technical.rom_ide: The sets archived under PC2286 and PC2386 share content. The four images 40189-2 through 40192-2 and the 64 KiB system reconstruction match byte for byte. This does not establish equivalent motherboards or validate compatibility.
